Kills `lex | while i < n: | if ch == ')' and not dq and stack and stack[-1][1] == 'paren': | int 1-1 #2`, which reads the BOTTOM of the stack: at the `)` the stack is [tick, paren], `stack[0][1]` is 'tick', so the paren never closes; the closing backtick then finds a paren on top, not a tick, and pushes a second tick; the end-of-line flush emits the unclosed paren as one span running to end of line, which swallows the outside `|| true`, so an unguarded capture reads as guarded. Valid bash (`bash -n` clean) with no stray `)` anywhere, which the earlier waiver claimed was required.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
n=$(grep -c foo f.txt || echo 0)
provenance: R10-T12 — `|| echo 0` substitutes a value and discards the status, so a failed grep reads as a clean zero. It is not a guard; only `|| true` (with `${n:-0}` at the point of use) and `|| :` are.
